description: Erection of front roof extensions to property nos. 61, 63, 65, 67 and 71 Lysia Street; excavation of part of the rear garden in connection with the enlargement of the existing basement and alterations to the front lightwell to include the installation of a single door to existing front bay window at basement level to no. 67 Lysia Street.
subdivision_of_building: Front roofs of 61, 63, 65, 67 & 71 Lysia Street and the basement of 67 Lysia Street
decision_conditions: Reason : 1 - The proposed front roof extensions at Nos. 61, 63, 65, 67 and 71 Lysia Street would result in visually prominent, overly bulky and discordant additions that would be out of keeping with the architectural character and appearance of the host properties and would disrupt the established roofline, form and uniform appearance of the terrace, to the detriment of the wider street scene. The proposal would therefore fail to preserve or enhance the character and appearance of the Crabtree Conservation Area, resulting in less than substantial harm to the significance of that designated heritage asset. The public benefits of the proposal are not considered sufficient to outweigh the identified heritage harm. As such, the proposal is contrary to Policies DC1, DC4 and DC8 of the Hammersmith & Fulham Local Plan (2018), Key Principles CAG2 and CAG3 of the Planning Guidance SPD (2018) and the National Planning Policy Framework.

Reason : 2 - The proposed basement excavation beneath the rear garden at No. 67 Lysia Street would extend beyond 50% of the depth of the host building, beyond 50% of the depth of the rear garden, and would not be set back from neighbouring boundaries where extending beyond the footprint of the host building. Furthermore, insufficient information has been submitted to demonstrate that the development would not adversely affect structural stability or increase flood risk. The proposal therefore fails to comply with the requirements of Policy DC11, CC3, CC4 of the Hammersmith & Fulham Local Plan (2018) and Key Principles BL2 and FR1 of the Planning Guidance SPD (2018).

Reason : 3 - In the absence of a site-specific Flood Risk Assessment, the Local Planning Authority cannot be satisfied that the development would provide an acceptable level of flood resilience, that risks from flooding have been properly assessed and mitigated, or that future occupiers, including those within the basement accommodation, would be safe for the lifetime of the development. The proposal therefore fails to comply with Policies CC3 and CC4 of the Local Plan (2018) and Key Principle FR1 of the Planning Guidance SPD (2018).
